alerts.title: John Henry Kirby Mansion
alerts.severity_label: Critical Alert: Sewer Disconnection + Asbestos Abatement
alerts.headline: City sewer disconnection permit (#26090093, issued 2026-10-14) paired with Texas DSHS asbestos abatement filing (#2026005825, scheduled 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-06).
alerts.preservation_note: Built in 1894 for businessman J.S. Price and purchased by lumber magnate John Henry Kirby in 1896, the 36-room Tudor Revival mansion at 2000 Smith Street achieved its landmark appearance in a 1928 remodeling designed by architect James Ruskin Bailey (1979 Preservation Houston Good Brick Award). A City of Houston sewer disconnection permit (#26090093, 'BLD DEMO/SEWER DISC', occupant '*KIRBY MANSION') was issued October 14, 2026 to applicant Robert Camacho, followed by Texas DSHS Notification #2026005825 scheduling abatement of 5,010 sq ft of Regulated Asbestos-Containing Material (RACM) from October 27 through November 6, 2026 by operator AAR Incorporated for owner OB Texas Properties LLC (Omair Bashir). Although the mansion lacks local Protected Landmark designation, Preservation Houston is actively monitoring the property and seeking dialogue with the owner.

dshs_notifications.work_description: Removal of asbestos containing white woven cloth, aircell pipe insulation, parapet, & wallboard utilizing wet methods, negative pressure, regulated area and air monitoring. Exterior window caulking removed utilizing open air methods. All ACM will be packaged and disposed of in accordance with applicable rules and regulations.

dshs_notifications.work_description: 1)Description of procedures to be followed in the event that unexpected asbestos is found or previously non-friable asbestos material becomes crumbled, pulverized, or reduced to powder: work will be stopped until an asbestos survey can be performed to confirm or deny the presence of asbestos 2)Description of planned demolition or abatement work, type of material, and method(s) to be used: 800 spot scrapes (approximately 0.25 sqft each) of spray applied fireproofing to be performed throughout building for the installation of new pipes, ducts and conduit. Abatement to be performed in negative pressure enclosures with a two stage decon and remote shower. Fireproofing to be adequately wet prior to removal. All waste to be disposed of as asbestos containing.

1) If unexpected asbestos containing materials are encountered, the work will immediately cease. The area will be misted with water, and the Asbestos Supervisor will notify the owner's and prime contractor's representatives for additional instructions. 2) The regulated asbestos containing material is primarily pipe insulation or other thermal system insulation. Piping consists of insulated piping and mudded elbows and associated fittings. Negative pressure containment and wet removal methods will be used for removal of TSI from piping and surface of a small tank. 3) To prevent migration of asbestos fibers from the work area, glove bags and negative pressure enclosures will be utilized. Poly containmnets will be constructed and poly sheeting will be use to wrap any remaining TSI on piping or small tank. Continuous negative pressure enclosures will be used during abatement activities, and clearance monitoring in the immediate work area will be performed following decontamination of enclosure. Waste will be double bagged, goose-necked, and labeled; the waste will be placed into a dedicated rolloff and manifested/transported to a permitted asbestos waste disposal site.
